This adapter allows Astro to deploy your [on-demand rendered routes and features](/en/guides/on-demand-rendering/) to [Cloudflare](https://www.cloudflare.com/), including [server islands](/en/guides/server-islands/), [actions](/en/guides/actions/), and [sessions](/en/guides/sessions/).

If you’re using Astro as a static site builder, you don’t need an adapter.

Learn how to deploy your Astro site in our [Cloudflare deployment guide](/en/guides/deploy/cloudflare/).

## Why Astro Cloudflare

[Section titled “Why Astro Cloudflare”](#why-astro-cloudflare)

Cloudflare’s [Developer Platform](https://developers.cloudflare.com/) lets you develop full-stack applications with access to resources such as storage and AI, all deployed to a global edge network. This adapter builds your Astro project for deployment through Cloudflare.

Astro includes an `astro add` command to automate the setup of official integrations. If you prefer, you can [install integrations manually](#manual-install) instead.

Add the Cloudflare adapter to enable server-rendering in your Astro project with the `astro add` command. This will install `@astrojs/cloudflare` and make the appropriate changes to your `astro.config.mjs` file in one step.

*   [npm](#tab-panel-0-0)
*   [pnpm](#tab-panel-0-1)
*   [Yarn](#tab-panel-0-2)

```
npx astro add cloudflare
```

Now, you can enable [on-demand rendering per page](/en/guides/on-demand-rendering/#enabling-on-demand-rendering), or set your build output configuration to `output: 'server'` to [server-render all your pages by default](/en/guides/on-demand-rendering/#server-mode).

1.  Add the `@astrojs/cloudflare` adapter to your project’s dependencies using your preferred package manager.
    
    *   [npm](#tab-panel-1-0)
    *   [pnpm](#tab-panel-1-1)
    *   [Yarn](#tab-panel-1-2)
    
    ```
    npm install @astrojs/cloudflare
    ```
    
2.  Add the adapter to your `astro.config.mjs` file:
    
    ```
    import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';import cloudflare from '@astrojs/cloudflare';export default defineConfig({  adapter: cloudflare(),});
    ```
    
3.  Astro will automatically generate a default configuration, using the package.json name field or the folder name as the Worker name. You can optionally create a [Wrangler configuration file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/) if you need custom settings. This example declares Cloudflare KV bindings:
    
    ```
    {  "name": "my-astro-app",  // Add your bindings here, e.g.:  // "kv_namespaces": [{ "binding": "MY_KV", "id": "<namespace_id>" }]}
    ```
    

The Cloudflare adapter accepts the following options from [`@cloudflare/vite-plugin`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/vite-plugin/):

*   `auxiliaryWorkers`
*   `configPath`
*   `inspectorPort`
*   `persistState`
*   `remoteBindings`
*   `experimental.headersAndRedirectsDevModeSupport`

It also accepts the following:

**Type:** `'passthrough' | 'cloudflare' | 'cloudflare-binding' | 'compile' | 'custom' | { build: 'compile' | 'cloudflare-binding', runtime?: 'cloudflare-binding' | 'passthrough' }`  
**Default:** `'cloudflare-binding'`

Determines which image service is used by the adapter. The adapter will default to `cloudflare-binding` mode when an incompatible image service is configured. Otherwise, it will use the globally configured image service:

*   **`cloudflare`:** Uses the [Cloudflare Image Resizing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/image-resizing/) service.
*   **`cloudflare-binding`:** Uses the [Cloudflare Images binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/transform-images/bindings/) for image transformation. The binding is automatically provisioned when you deploy.
*   **`passthrough`:** Uses the existing [`noop`](/en/guides/images/#configure-no-op-passthrough-service) service.
*   **`compile`:** Uses the [configured image service](/en/reference/configuration-reference/#imageservice) or falls back to a combination of internal dependencies to transform images locally at build time for prerendered routes. The noop `passthrough` option is configured for on-demand rendered pages.
*   **`custom`:** Uses the [configured image service](/en/reference/configuration-reference/#imageservice) (defaults to Sharp) to process assets at build time for prerendered routes. Bundles the image service for runtime image handling, without checking its compatibility with Cloudflare’s `workerd` runtime.

**Added in:** `@astrojs/cloudflare@14.2.0`

You can also configure the image service as an object by providing a build-time service (`compile` or `cloudflare-binding`) and, optionally, a runtime service (`passthrough` or `cloudflare-binding`).

When the runtime service is omitted, its default value depends on the configured build-time service. It falls back to `'passthrough'` for `build: 'compile'` and to `'cloudflare-binding'` for `build: 'cloudflare-binding'`.

```
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';import cloudflare from '@astrojs/cloudflare';export default defineConfig({  adapter: cloudflare({    imageService: { build: 'compile', runtime: 'cloudflare-binding' }  }),});
```

Using `imageService: 'cloudflare-binding'` enables image optimization using the [Cloudflare Images binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/transform-images/bindings/) only at runtime.

To opt in to build-time image optimization with the binding during `workerd` prerendering, set `build` to `'cloudflare-binding'`. If the binding fails to transform an image at build time, the adapter falls back to the [configured image service](/en/reference/configuration-reference/#imageservice) (defaults to Sharp).

```
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';import cloudflare from '@astrojs/cloudflare';export default defineConfig({  adapter: cloudflare({    imageService: { build: 'cloudflare-binding', runtime: 'cloudflare-binding' }  }),});
```

## Activation Contract

Load when the SessionStart hook injects "Learning mode", a repository needs classifying, the user asks for learning notes in the vault (`[local path]`), or asks a conceptual question ("¿qué es X?", "explicame X", "what is X").

## Hard Rules

- The vault is LEARNING documentation, never a copy of repo docs: explain why/how, mental models, tradeoffs. Link to repo files instead of duplicating.
- Modes: `learn` = full notes + concept links + exam offer at milestones (`project-exam`); `log` = decisions note and concept links only; `off` = nothing for the project.
- Notes in neutral Spanish, short paragraphs, project examples. Keep **[V]** (verified) and **[A]** (inference).
- Notes are not versioned: update in place, bump `actualizado:`.
- Decisions keep a dated `Historial` (see references); tell the user in chat, in one or two lines, what changed and why.
- Never interrupt mid-task for doubts: collect them and ask once at task close, as one multi-select question.
- Concepts: search `Concepts/` (filenames and `aliases`) before creating; update the existing note instead of duplicating. Link concepts IN-BODY at first mention. No manual project lists in concept notes (backlinks do that).
- Classification question: ALWAYS present all three options (learn, log, off) with one-line meanings. Never omit, filter or preselect any, even if a vault folder already exists.
- Conceptual questions are saved in ANY session: any mode including `off`, any directory, outside git repos. It is the user's learning, not the project's. After answering, save it and tell the user in one line ("Guardé *Lint* en Concepts"). Inside a learn/log project, also link the project note.
- `Concepts/` has two sizes. "Término": 3-5 lines (qué es, ejemplo, dónde apareció), `assets/termino.md`, `tags: [termino]`. "Concepto": full `assets/concepto.md`, `tags: [concepto]`. A término grows into a concepto in place (same file, change the tag) when it deepens.
- Never write repository files or project notes in `off` mode.

## Decision Gates

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Hook says no learning mode | Ask ONE question with all three options (learn / log / off + one-line meanings), then `set`; for learn/log create the folder |
| Conceptual question (any mode or directory) | Answer, then create/update a término in `Concepts/`; one-line notice |
| Task closed with new module, architecture change, decision, gotcha or concept | Update notes per mode |
| Trivial change (rename, typo, formatting) | Skip |
| Concept deserves depth | Create or grow from `assets/concepto.md` |
| Project for the user's job at UAP | Folder `Projects/UAP/<Project>/`; otherwise `Projects/<Name>/` |

## Execution Steps

1. Registry: `node "[local path]" set <learn|log|off> --folder "Projects/<Name>" --name "<Name>" --cwd "<repo>"`; read with `get --cwd "<repo>"`. Worktrees share the main repo entry.
2. New project folder, diagrams and decision history format: see `references/project-setup.md`.
3. After each task: update affected notes, then concepts and in-body links.
4. At task close ask collected doubts once; in `learn`, offer `project-exam` at milestones.
5. Agent rules for non-Claude agents live in `references/agent-rules.md`, synced into each agent's instruction file with `node "[local path]"`. Re-sync after editing that file.

## Output Contract

Report in chat: notes created/updated (paths), decisions changed, concepts saved, doubts asked. No other prose.

## References

- `assets/concepto.md`, `assets/termino.md`, `assets/proyecto-indice.md`, `assets/decisiones.md`
- `references/agent-rules.md`, `references/project-setup.md`, `../project-exam/SKILL.md`

- Latency budget: "the <= 3.0 s transcription budget." (`socra/server/README.md`, Whisper benchmark section, around line 205)
- Piper voice is about 79 MB. (`socra/server/README.md:42`)

## Problem

University settings need a low-cost, reproducible robot arm for laparoscopic surgery training by teleoperation. Laparoscopic tools pivot about a fixed point at the incision, the remote center of motion (RCM). The client asked for that constraint to be held by software.

## Constraints

- Reuse hardware that was already bought: three NEMA17 motors, DRV8825 drivers, a RAMPS 1.6 board, a 12 V supply, an Arduino Mega, two ESP32 boards and servos.
- A tight deadline.
- A team of three.

## Decisions

- **Closed-form inverse kinematics in C++ headers.** It is cheap enough to run in a control loop on a microcontroller. Checked two ways: forward kinematics against the live CAD model to 0.003 mm, and an IK round-trip error of 0.0004 mm over 32k poses.
- **Tool-space resolved-rate control with damped least squares and an adaptive damping factor**, so the arm stays controllable near singularities. On x86 it takes 0.123 µs per cycle, with 0 joint-limit violations in 200k cycles. It was not measured on the ESP32.
- **Check feasibility before building.** The Jacobian has rank exactly 2 over 3000 poses, so the RCM cannot be held in software with this arm. The best pseudo-RCM had a median error of 101 mm (219 mm over the full range).
- **Move on after the negative result.** A structural fix was proposed (add a linear axis, remove joint 3), but it was never built. It was superseded on 2026-09-10 by a 6-DOF software-RCM design with six motors.
- **A browser 3D simulator** (canvas, no libraries) to look at poses before touching hardware.

## What I owned

The Fusion 360 model and joint geometry, the IK and controller headers, the analysis behind the 6-DOF redesign. I worked in a team of three.

The receiver firmware file (receiver.cpp) was written by an AI, not by me.

## Result

- Kinematics and control run in simulation, with the numbers above. The controller timing was measured on x86 only.
- The analysis showed that the original four-DOF arm cannot hold an RCM in software. That redirected the design to six axes.
- No mechanical design of our own has been built yet. Joint limits and link lengths are assumptions.

## Problem

University settings need a low-cost, reproducible robot arm to train laparoscopic surgery by teleoperation. Laparoscopic tools pivot about a fixed point at the incision, the remote center of motion (RCM). The plan was to hold that point in software.

## Constraints

- Reuse hardware that was already bought: NEMA17 stepper motors, DRV8825 drivers, a RAMPS 1.6 board, an Arduino Mega and two ESP32 boards.
- A tight deadline and a team of three.

## Decisions

- **Closed-form analytic inverse kinematics in C++**, with no iterative solver to tune or converge, so it fits comfortably inside the 50 Hz control loop.
- **Tool-space resolved-rate control**, so the operator moves the instrument tip and the controller works out the joints.
- **Check feasibility numerically before building the constraint.** Five independent numerical checks, instead of trusting one model.
- **Report the negative result** instead of shipping a fake constraint.
- **A browser 3D simulator**, so the team and the client can operate the arm without hardware.
- **Automate the CAD work.** Assembly and measurements in Fusion 360 through its Python API.

## What I owned

We built the arm as a team of three, without a fixed split of tasks. My focus was the control software and simulation: the C++ motion layer, the feasibility analysis, the simulator and the Fusion 360 automation.

## Result

- Inverse kinematics validated against the CAD model to 3 micrometres, at 0.1% of the 50 Hz control loop, unit tested and warning-clean.
- Showed that the planned software RCM was unreachable on the built hardware, two degrees of freedom short, and found a structural fix that yields all four laparoscopic degrees of freedom with no extra motors.
- A simulator the team and the client use to operate the arm without hardware.

name: gentle-ui-design
description: "Trigger: product interface design, web UI, design critique, browsing experience, responsive layout. Guide usable interfaces for the current project."
license: Apache-2.0
metadata:
  author: gentleman-programming
  version: "1.0"
---

## Activation Contract

Use for web and product interfaces when shaping, implementing, or assessing a user experience. Pair with `gentle-design` when producing artboards: gentle-design owns delivery, this skill owns UX quality. Use `gentle-ai-tui-design` for terminal interfaces.

## Hard Rules

- Keep a read-only critique read-only; do not install tools or dependencies for this guidance.
- Establish the user's job and success condition before appearance. Ask only when missing intent would materially change a decision.
- Reuse the project's brand, components, and platform conventions; avoid universal aesthetic bans.
- Do not invent evidence or conceal inaccessible controls. Model real content ranges and states; this guidance adds no hooks, detectors, or mandatory tool chains.

## Decision Gates

| Need or symptom | Load and apply |
| --- | --- |
| Unclear purpose, weak copy, or generic direction | `references/task-and-content.md` |
| Search, large collections, or difficult comparison | `references/browse-and-compare.md` |
| Flat hierarchy, clutter, or weak feedback | `references/composition-and-feedback.md` |
| Narrow screens, input access, or missing states | `references/adaptive-interfaces.md` |

## Execution Steps

1. Identify the audience, primary job, constraints, and likely content sizes; inspect existing project conventions when available.
2. Load only the relevant references and select defaults or justified exceptions for the task.
3. Apply the project's visual language and account for touch, keyboard, focus, contrast, and reduced motion.
4. Inspect visually when useful and authorized; report observations rather than implying an inspection occurred.

## Output Contract

Summarize design choices and tradeoffs, files changed if any, checks actually performed, and important unknowns.

## References

- `references/task-and-content.md` — purpose, information architecture, art direction, and truthful copy.
- `references/browse-and-compare.md` — search, collection scale, comparison, and navigation state.
- `references/composition-and-feedback.md` — hierarchy, density, color, type, and visual feedback.
- `references/adaptive-interfaces.md` — responsive behavior, accessible interaction, and states.

# Task and content

## Start with the job

Choose the first screen by what the person needs to do, not by a favorite page template.
A single product may contain several of these jobs; identify the leading job for the current surface.

| Job | Give priority to | A useful outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Find | Search scope, filters, recognizable results | Reach the intended item without inspecting every entry |
| Compare | Shared attributes and a stable order | Understand meaningful differences before choosing |
| Act | Current state, the primary action, and consequences | Complete the operation without losing context |
| Read | A clear heading, readable text, and wayfinding | Understand the information and find a passage again |
| Decide | The proposition, relevant evidence, and next step | Make a choice with the information available |

For a work surface, put the working controls and current material in the initial viewport.
A large promotional hero ahead of an existing user's records makes a routine action take longer.
A compact orientation banner can help a new user, but it should not permanently displace the work.
For a public introduction, a prominent opening can instead explain what the offering does and for whom.

Arrange navigation around the objects and tasks people recognize.
For example, a shared workshop app could group **Reservations**, **Tools**, and **Members** rather than burying them under internal department names.
Keep the main action near its object: **Reserve tool** belongs with availability, not inside an unrelated settings menu.
If an action has an irreversible consequence, show that consequence before it is committed.
Avoid showing several equally prominent primary actions when one is the normal next step; preserve alternatives as clearly labeled secondary actions.

## Specific, truthful content

Use exact labels that predict the outcome and match what the system actually does.
A generic label forces the user to open or guess; a specific one makes the choice legible.

| Weak | Better when accurate | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Continue` | `Review reservation` | Names the next stage without promising completion |
| `Manage` | `Change pickup time` | Explains which operation is available |
| `Something went wrong` | `Reservation not saved. Try again.` | States the consequence and a useful next action |
| `The future of shared spaces` | `Book workshop tools for your next project` | Identifies the audience's activity |

Do not invent customer identities, quotes, usage figures, charts, or claims of measured results.
Use real evidence only when it is available and appropriate to disclose.
Label illustrative records as demonstration data and avoid presenting them as actual customers or outcomes.
If no evidence exists, explain the capability plainly instead of manufacturing social proof.
When the actual next action depends on missing product intent, ask that focused question rather than assembling a broad questionnaire.

## Give the interface a reasoned visual idea

Take a cue from the subject and make it useful across the surface, not just in a headline.
For a workshop booking page, a calm timetable with clear availability can express the practical, shared nature of the service;
for a reading archive, a quiet index and legible excerpts may communicate its purpose more effectively.
Use the project's established palette, type, shapes, and components as the starting vocabulary.
A coherent direction comes from decisions about emphasis, content, and layout, not merely from removing shadows or decoration.

Inventory authentic material already available before deciding that a design needs prominent imagery.
An accurate diagram, product image, or real document can explain an offering; a fabricated screenshot or unrelated stock image can mislead.
When suitable assets are unavailable, use a purposeful text-led composition instead of pretending the product has imagery it does not.
Do not fetch remote assets automatically. If sourcing is explicitly authorized, track the relevant usage rights.

Let content dictate whether sections vary or repeat.
A narrative can change rhythm when its subject changes; a sequence of comparable options benefits from the same structure.
Neither a different layout for every section nor identical blocks everywhere is a universal rule.
# Composition and feedback

## Establish hierarchy

Give each text role a job: page title identifies the place, section headings describe groups,
body text carries information, and labels name controls. Make these roles visibly distinct using the existing type system.
When every line is bold and oversized, users cannot tell which element leads; reserve the strongest emphasis for the current task or heading.
A dense incident list may need compact headings; a long policy explanation needs more comfortable measure and line-height.
Do not replace the project's fonts merely to follow a trend.

Use alignment to make relationships visible. Align comparable numeric columns consistently,
and keep units and precision understandable; do not make `9`, `12`, and `105` difficult to compare through inconsistent placement.
Use a consistent left edge for related labels and values unless the content or reading direction calls for another arrangement.
Allow headings to wrap naturally instead of forcing an arbitrary line count.

For a hypothetical interface, a 16px body with a 24px line-height and a modestly larger section heading can be a starting example,
not a brand token or universal scale. Check the actual font, content, platform, and viewport.
Likewise, repeated 8px and 16px spacing might create a useful rhythm in one project;
use existing tokens first and adjust the relationship when the content needs it.
Optically balance the whole composition: a short title and a dense table need different surrounding space,
without enforcing arbitrary percentages or symmetrical empty areas.

## Group without visual noise

This skill gives you the tools and permission to make design that earns the name out-of-distribution craft. Work as an award-winning design director would: production-grade code, a clear POV, a deep grasp of what the client and its users need, and exceptional craft.

Core principles:
- Finish the job. No hedging, no shortcuts: the deliverable is complete, except assets the user must provide.
- Scale ambition to the surface's mode (see Modes). Persuade and Experience get full commitment: bold, distinct work with a point of view. On Operate and Read, ambition shows as precision and restraint, and patterns the visitor already knows earn their place.
- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at, and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again, rather than screenshotting after every tweak.

## Setup

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md, DESIGN.md, the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface or replacement visual world. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.
3. After resolving analysis and direction, read [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, including small refinements. It carries the quality floor, the absolute bans, and the reflexes no detector catches. Do not load it for planning-only work.

**Launcher unavailable:** On refusal or failure, send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, including reading [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.

# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here except a line marked as a ban; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12–16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

d2d4c97 docs: record the P2 decision in PLAN.md

Exploded index is now the chosen design, and I've polished it with impeccable. P2 is closed. The canvas is refreshed at the same URL:

**http://127.0.0.1:2401/[REDACTED]/d/portfolio-directions/**

**What the polish changed**
- **Labels above headings removed:** "Assembly drawing · Cover" above your name, "Leg A/B" above the two legs, and "Sheet N" next to every section heading. Each heading now stands alone, and the numbered marker beside it still ties it to the side map.
- **Browser defaults themed to match the palette:** text selection, scrollbar, text cursor, link underlines (offset, and thicker on hover) and tabular numerals in the table and progress caption.
- **Header:** the email now uses the normal font, since the code-style font was only there to look technical. On a phone, the header shrinks from three rows to two: with JS on, the address text is hidden behind the "Copy email" button; without JS it still shows.
- **About section:** one "DRAFT" tag instead of two.

**Checks**
- **Screenshots:** I looked at the result in dark and light at 1440 px and in the 390 px phone layout. Nothing overflows sideways on the phone.
- **Scroll effects:** I measured them again after the polish, and they still work. Drawings draw in as they rise into view, the side map lifts the current layer, and the progress line fills down the page.
- **Privacy scan:** the file has no local paths and no plain email address.
- **impeccable detector:** I ran it once on the final file, as the skill prescribes. It still flags two things, and I left both on purpose:
  - **The grid background:** it's the blueprint drafting grid that powers the hover effect you asked for.
  - **The first leg column has no inner padding:** its text lines up with the left edge of the hero and the parts table.

**Two notes for P3**
- **Display font:** impeccable recommends a self-hosted display font instead of the system font. These mockups can't load font files, so I'll choose and self-host one when building the real site in P3, and check its license first.
- **Product brief:** the project has no `PRODUCT.md` yet. `/impeccable init` can write one: a short interview that records the product context future design passes read. It's optional.

Everything is committed (`2e34434`, `d2d4c97`), and `PLAN.md` records the decision. Next is **P3**: building the real Astro site from this design, with your projects, CV data and posts. Should I start?
